questions.subject: HUMAN_GEOGRAPHY
questions.topic: Greenbelt and the land price just outside it
questions.learningObjective: Explain why land just outside a greenbelt is expensive
questions.stem: Why is land just outside a greenbelt often more expensive than land farther away?

options.text: It is the nearest developable land to the city, so demand concentrates there
It is cheaper because the greenbelt lowers nearby demand
It is protected land with no development rights
options.misconception: confuses outside with inside the belt

options.text: It has lower transport access than fringe land

questions.explanation: Land just outside the belt is the nearest developable land, so demand concentrates and prices rise. Protected status applies inside, not outside.
questions.hint: Nearest developable land draws demand.

questions.subject: HUMAN_GEOGRAPHY
questions.topic: Land price just outside a greenbelt
questions.learningObjective: Predict price change when a greenbelt tightens
questions.stem: A city tightens its greenbelt, shrinking the developable fringe. In stage one, what happens to land price just outside the belt?

options.text: It falls as the belt pushes demand inward only
It rises as developable land becomes scarcer
It stays flat because belts do not affect prices
options.misconception: denies the price effect of scarcity

options.text: It halves as development stops entirely
options.misconception: overstates the stop; development concentrates, not ceases

questions.explanation: A tighter belt makes developable land scarcer, so prices just outside rise. Demand is not pushed only inward.
questions.hint: Scarcer developable land means higher price.

questions.stem: What is leapfrog development?

options.text: Development that stays strictly inside the belt
Development that fills every vacant lot in sequence
Development that skips over vacant land to build farther out
Development that moves only along transit lines

questions.explanation: Leapfrog development skips vacant land to build farther out, leaving gaps. Infill and contained growth are different patterns.
questions.hint: Skipping land to build farther out.

questions.topic: Polycentric city and why it emerges
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a polycentric city emerges
questions.stem: Explain why a polycentric city tends to emerge as a metro area grows.

answer.exemplar: As a metro grows, congestion and high central costs push firms and residents to secondary centres, which develop their own jobs and services, creating multiple centres.

questions.explanation: Growth raises central costs and congestion, encouraging secondary centres. These then attract their own jobs and services.
questions.hint: Congestion and cost push growth to new centres.
